name: OGLE-SMC-ECL-1421 A
description: The primary star of the eclipsing binary OGLE-SMC-ECL-1421, 2.72 solar masses and 17.7 solar radii; the two stars eclipse each other every 102.834 days.

radius.source: Primary radius (solar radii) 17.7 +/- 0.3, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Graczyk et al. (2020ApJ...904...13G)

mass.source: Primary mass (solar masses) 2.72 +/- 0.02, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Graczyk et al. (2020ApJ...904...13G)

temperature.source: Primary log Teff 3.732 +/- 0.008, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Graczyk et al. (2020ApJ...904...13G): 5395 K

gravity.source: Primary log g 2.37 +/- 0.01, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Graczyk et al. (2020ApJ...904...13G)

distance.source: Graczyk et al. (2020), ApJ 904, 13, the distance to OGLE-SMC-ECL-1421: 62.03 +/- 0.64 kpc

text.card: The primary star of OGLE-SMC-ECL-1421, a pair that eclipse each other every 102.834 days.
text.introduction: It has 2.72 solar masses and 17.7 solar radii; its partner has 2.85 and 23.8, measured from the eclipses and the stars' motions.
text.locator: DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164), OGLE-SMC-ECL-1421: Mass, Radius and Period, from Graczyk et al. (2020ApJ...904...13G)

notes: Masses, radii and temperatures as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) (https://www.astro.keele.ac.uk/jkt/debcat/) lists them from Graczyk et al. (2020ApJ...904...13G); Graczyk et al. (2014ApJ...780...59G).
SIMBAD knows the system as OGLE SMC-ECL-1421 but links no Gaia DR3 source; it is placed at the Gaia DR3 source 0.02 arcsec from SIMBAD's position, G = 16.97 against DEBCat's V = 17.18.

radialVelocity.source: No catalogued radial velocity: Gaia DR3 measures none for source 4688970798174366464 and SIMBAD lists none. Zero is assumed; a 30 km/s error moves the star by one part in 20,000,000 of its distance per century
